rationale: The workflow runs two independent lint/style jobs (eslint and code-style) with no job-level timeout, so a hung or runaway step can consume unbounded runner time. The retrieved experiment evidence (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508, pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT) measured a comparable Checks workflow (checkout, setup-node, npm ci, lint/typecheck steps) and showed adding timeout-minutes: 5 reduced median elapsed time by 26.8% while preserving all checks and successes. This workflow already applies path filtering and concurrency cancellation, so the remaining supported, minimal optimization is to bound each job with an explicit timeout. Adding timeout-minutes: 5 to both jobs preserves every existing step and required check, introduces no new actions, secrets, network access, or publishing/deployment operations, and does not weaken permissions. A 5-minute budget is generous for lint/prettier-style jobs and bounds runaway consumption without removing coverage.
